To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the media is a key site for the construction of mythology and the dissemination of ideology.

the media is a powerful ideological agent that constructs and reinforces myths that are based on a series of interrelated and overlapping archetypal narratives that are used to justify and promote the status quo and to marginalize those that are perceived as a threat.
The media’s representation of the 7 July 2005 attacks on London is a form of mythology that is used by journalists to construct a narrative of the event.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the discourse of media texts constructs and perpetuates myths, which function as ideological vehicles.
the ideological role of media discourse and its relationship with mythology and ideology.
the ideological role of mythological discourse, which is a form of discourse that is characterised by a set of archetypal, conventionalised and culturally specific narrative structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DMA offers a systematic framework to researchers in the fields of journalism, media and culture studies, as well as critical discourse studies.
my previous work on mythology and ideology in the media has been a prelude to the development and proposal of a new approach to critical discourse analysis.
DMA is an analytical framework that combines the theoretical and methodoligical perspectives of CDA with the analytical tools of mythological criticism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing an approach that is able to identify, interpret and analyse the ideological role of mythological archetypes in the discourse of the media, politics and culture.
it is the application of CDA to the study of mythology, ideology and discourse.
DMA is a critical approach to the analysis of mythology and ideology in the media that draws upon CDA and the work of Roland Barthes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should not underestimate the power and influence of mythology and the ways in which it functions as a vehicle for ideology.
discourse, ideology and mythology are not separate or unrelated phenomena but are interrelated and overlapping in the construction and analysis of media texts.
discourse is not simply a vehicle for ideology.
